newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares slide, seen falling further.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares slide, seen falling further.

text.p: Slovenian shares eased a further 0.81 percent on Thursday on low turnover and traders said the general pessimism in the market could continue into next week.
"There is apathy in our market -- next week there could be some turning point, but it is hard to say what direction prices will go then," Jernej Obed, trader at A bank said.
The SBI index fell 11.14 points to 1,367.64, its fourth consecutive day of decline. The blue-chip index has fallen 4.43 percent since the start of the week alone.

The Bank of Slovenia said last month that international investors would have to open custodian accounts at one of 14 fully-licenced local banks in order to trade in Slovenia's securities. Since then, the SBI index has shed 17.4 percent.

"Prices will definitely continue falling slowly until foreign investors return to the market. Some traders expect that could happen next week when banks reveal the costs of opening such accounts," Obed said.
"But if costs are too high, foreigners won't come back and the situation could get even worse," he added.
Banks have indicated that the cost of maintaining the new accounts was likely to be about 12 percent of the amount handled.
Overall six shares fell, seven rose and 13 were untraded. Turnover fell to 54.6 million tolars from 109.8 million.
Bank SKB was the most actively traded share, easing 0.61 percent to 56,850 tolars on volume of 259 shares for total turnover of 14.7 million tolars.
Brokerage Primofin was the leading decliner, tumbling 9.79 percent to 12,900 tolars on volume of just three shares.
Ordinary shares of bank Hmezad were the biggest gainers, firming 3.85 percent to 13,500 tolars on volume of 25 shares. -- Novica Mihajlovic, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
